title: Classic Korean Pear Beef Bulgogi
shortDescription: Thin slices of beef marinated with Korean pear, soy sauce, garlic, scallions, and toasted sesame, then quickly grilled in small batches.
culturalContext: Bulgogi is a broad Korean preparation of thin marinated meat cooked over fire or on a hot surface. Pear is one established marinade option, but sweetness, aromatics, cut, and cooking method vary by cook and household; this draft makes no singular origin claim.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

totalTime.display: 2 hours 40 minutes, including minimum marination and rest

equipment: Nonreactive mixing bowl or food-safe zip bag
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill

ingredients.preparation: partially frozen, then sliced 3 mm / 1/8 inch thick against the grain

mixOrder: Whisk soy sauce and brown sugar until the sugar begins to dissolve.
Stir in grated pear, onion, garlic, ginger, scallions, pepper, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive glass or stainless-steel bowl, or a food-safe zip bag set on a rimmed tray
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: For 3 mm / 1/8-inch slices, do not exceed 24 hours; extended exposure to pear and salt can make the surface overly soft and strongly seasoned.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: If marinade is wanted as a finishing sauce, portion it into a separate saucepan before adding raw beef.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade that contacted raw beef. A separately reserved portion may be served; do not brush used marinade onto cooked meat.
substitutions: A ripe Bosc pear may replace Korean pear by weight, but sweetness and tenderizing effect will differ.
Certified gluten-free tamari may replace soy sauce only after every label is checked.
allergenNotes: Most regular soy sauce contains wheat; verify labels for gluten needs.

instructions.heading: Slice the beef
instructions.action: Firm the beef in the freezer for 20 to 30 minutes, then slice it 3 mm / 1/8 inch thick against the grain. Keep the sliced beef refrigerated while making the marinade.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices are flexible, evenly thin, and show short cross-sections of the muscle grain.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean cutting board; wash hands and sanitize the knife, board, and counter after raw-beef contact.

instructions.heading: Mix the pear marinade
instructions.action: Whisk soy sauce and brown sugar, then stir in pear, onion, garlic, ginger, scallions, pepper, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The sugar is mostly dissolved and the mixture is loose and evenly speckled.
instructions.safetyNote: Reserve any portion intended for serving before the marinade touches raw beef.

instructions.heading: Marinate under refrigeration
instructions.action: Coat the beef thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for 2 to 12 hours. Turn the bag or stir once midway if practical.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every slice is lightly coated without dry pockets.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate at room temperature; discard raw-contact marinade after the beef is removed.

instructions.heading: Preheat and arrange
instructions.action: Preheat the approved grill to medium-high. Clean and lightly oil the grate, then let excess marinade drip from the beef so it sears instead of steams.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The surface is hot enough for an immediate active sizzle.
instructions.safetyNote: Use an outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric appliance only, with required ventilation and clearances.

instructions.heading: Grill in small batches
instructions.action: Spread the beef in a single layer and grill, turning and separating the slices, until browned and cooked through, about 2 to 4 minutes per batch.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Edges are browned, the meat is no longer raw-looking, and the thickest practical cluster reaches the target temperature.
instructions.safetyNote: Use separate clean utensils and platter for cooked beef; time and color alone are not the doneness test.

instructions.heading: Rest and serve
instructions.action: Transfer the beef to a clean platter and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving with rice, ssam greens, and reviewed banchan.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Juices settle and the beef remains glossy rather than watery.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not return cooked beef to the raw-meat bowl or pour raw-contact marinade over it.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high, about 400–450°F / 204–232°C. Follow the appliance manual for clearance and ventilation; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion, followed by a 3-minute rest
visualDonenessCues: Thin slices are browned at the edges and no longer look raw.
The thickest practical cluster reaches 145°F / 63°C before the 3-minute rest.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw beef and its marinade separate from ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize contacted surfaces.
Use separate raw and cooked plates and utensils, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
Measure the thickest practical portion with a calibrated food thermometer; grill marks and time alone do not establish doneness.
For whole-cut beef, reach 145°F / 63°C and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use; follow ventilation and clearance instructions.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Use ripe Bosc pear by weight when Korean pear is unavailable; do not substitute pineapple or kiwi at the same marination time because their enzymes can soften thin beef rapidly.
Use certified gluten-free tamari only after label review; sesame requires a separate reviewed reformulation rather than a simple omission claim.
ingredientSourcing: Ask a Korean market or butcher for thin bulgogi-cut ribeye or sirloin, or partially freeze and slice at home.
Choose a heavy, fragrant Korean/Asian pear without soft or leaking spots.
Use plain toasted sesame oil rather than an unverified flavored blend.
makeAhead: Mix the marinade up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate it before raw contact. Slice and marinate the beef 2 to 12 hours before cooking; do not hold the thin beef in pear marinade longer than 24 hours.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef within 2 hours in a shallow airtight container at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 3 days.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Reheat only the portion needed and avoid prolonged cooking that toughens thin beef.
leftovers: Use leftover beef in a rice bowl or lettuce wrap after reheating to 165°F / 74°C; keep fresh garnishes separate until serving.
servingSuggestions: Serve with steamed rice, ssam greens, kimchi, and ssamjang whose allergens have been checked.
Offer raw garlic or chile only as optional accompaniments and keep them away from the raw-meat work area.

faq.question: Can I cook this without an outdoor grill?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill or a heavy skillet under effective kitchen ventilation. Do not bring charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.

faq.question: Why is the beef partially frozen before slicing?
faq.answer: Brief chilling firms the meat so thin, even slices are easier to cut; it is a slicing technique, not a food-safety kill step.
